check_text:
protocol.py: 1 biology problem (1 error).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 9 stocks
   line 62:  p20.aspirate(10, source_plate[src])
   At line 62 the tip went into A12 (well A12 in slot 2), B11 (well B11 in slot 2), C4 (well
   C4 in slot 2), C7 (well C7 in slot 2) and 5 more while it still carried A12 (well A12 in
   slot 2), B3 (well B3 in slot 2), B11 (well B11 in slot 2), C7 (well C7 in slot 2) and 5
   more from an earlier step (this line did it 9 times). A tip that has touched one liquid
   leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material
   that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from them then took the unwanted material along
   into 9 other wells: wells A2, B1, B2, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and 1 more in slot 3.
   Affected: wells A12, B11, C4, C7, D1, E5, F9, G2 and 1 more in slot 2.
   Also reached 9 other wells: wells A2, B1, B2, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1 and 1 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 62 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [4f06a795004c]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
